understanding: The supplied code partially recovers a Raft library with separate main-loop, replication, FSM, and snapshot responsibilities. Observed mechanisms include voter-index aggregation, candidate vote tallying, asynchronous application handoff, configuration replacement, snapshot installation, and snapshot publication followed by log reclamation. Application interfaces describe stronger semantic expectations than queue admission or progress metadata alone establishes. Constructor selection, replication acknowledgments, startup recovery, future completion, and several storage semantics remain unread. This inventory describes implementation behavior and evidence gaps; it establishes neither correctness nor a defect.

target_profile.system_boundary: The hashicorp/raft library, including supplied protocol code and available repository storage and transport implementations. Client FSM logic is outside the library boundary, while library callback scheduling and completion handling remain inside it. External storage backends mentioned in README.md are outside the supplied implementation evidence.
protocol_contexts: Raft follower, candidate, and leader roles with term and log-index context.
Protocol-version-dependent RPC admission and membership encoding.
Candidate campaigns with optional pre-vote and a leadership-transfer bypass.
Leader commitment objects with voter membership and a startIndex threshold.
FSM execution, snapshot capture, remote snapshot installation, and log reclamation.
external_interfaces: Apply, ApplyLog, Barrier, and VerifyLeader return futures.
Transport supplies RPC channels, outbound RPC methods, peer encoding, and an optional heartbeat fast path.
WithPreVote is an optional transport extension.
FSM supplies Apply, Snapshot, and Restore; BatchingFSM optionally supplies ApplyBatch.
Observed storage calls include StoreLogs, GetLog, DeleteRange, snapshot Create/Open, and sink Close/Cancel.
ownership: runCandidate handles candidate events on the main loop.
commitment serializes its voter map and commit index using a mutex.
processLogs schedules work to runFSM through fsmMutateCh.
runFSM owns local lastIndex and lastTerm variables used for snapshot capture.
takeSnapshot requests FSM state and main-thread configuration through separate futures.
FileSnapshotSink owns file finalization, metadata publication, directory rename, and snapshot reaping.
selection_injection: The FSM interface explicitly assigns application implementation to library clients.
runFSM selects BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore behavior using runtime type assertions.
installSnapshot selects complete old-log removal when the supplied log store reports MonotonicLogStore.IsMonotonic().
Transport permits heartbeat handling either through a callback or the normal consumer channel.
Constructor wiring and active storage/transport selection have not been supplied; injection does not exclude repository implementations from this inventory.
variants: Pre-vote enabled versus disabled; leadership transfer bypasses pre-vote.
Membership entries use deprecated peer encoding below protocol version 2 and LogConfiguration otherwise.
Single-entry FSM callbacks versus ApplyBatch; optional ConfigurationStore.
Monotonic log-store reset versus trailing-log compaction after snapshot installation.
File snapshot synchronization varies with noSync and operating system.
File lookup lists in-memory, discard, cache, network, and TCP implementations whose contents remain unread.
unknowns: NewRaft construction, channel setup, startup recovery, and actual adapter activation.
StableStore and LogStore contracts, partial-write behavior, and built-in implementation details.
Replication reply validation and association with term, peer identity, and log contents.

activities.purpose: Admit log work, aggregate replica support, and advance decision progress.
activities.realization_summary: ApplyLog hands off futures; dispatchLogs assigns log identities and calls local storage; commitment aggregates reported voter indexes. The leader loop consuming commitment notifications and remote support producers are unread.

activities.purpose: Acquire and change local authority and protocol context.
activities.realization_summary: runCandidate distinguishes pre-vote, election, newer-term fallback, and election timeout. RPC header admission checks protocol versions. State and term setter implementations remain unread.

activities.purpose: Restore replica state and resume participation from retained history.
activities.realization_summary: installSnapshot stores incoming bytes, waits for an FSM restore future, replaces progress and configuration metadata, and attempts log cleanup. Restart and incremental catch-up are not recovered.
unknowns: Restore dispatch in the unread FSM loop tail

activities.purpose: Represent and activate participant changes for protocol consumers.
activities.realization_summary: appendConfigurationEntry constructs a next configuration, dispatches its entry, replaces latest configuration and commitment voters, and changes replication. Snapshot installation replaces both latest and committed configuration.

activities.purpose: Schedule decided history and invoke application effects.
activities.realization_summary: processLogs prepares ordered entries and sends batches to the FSM channel, then updates lastApplied. runFSM invokes single or batch callbacks and responds to associated futures. Client state-machine logic is external, but scheduling remains local.

activities.purpose: Persist and reclaim logs and snapshot recovery representations.
activities.realization_summary: Local log storage precedes local match reporting. takeSnapshot persists and closes a sink before updating snapshot metadata and compacting logs. FileSnapshotSink has explicit finalization, publication, reaping, and repeat-close branches.
unknowns: Storage partial failures and crash recovery
Repeated Close interpretation after an earlier failure

activities.purpose: Expose admission, completion, barriers, and authority checks to callers.
activities.realization_summary: ApplyLog and Barrier distinguish enqueue timeout, shutdown, and channel handoff. Candidate processing rejects leader-only requests. FSM processing supplies callback responses to futures. Public comments distinguish ambiguous leadership loss from restore abortion.
